newsitem.title: CHINA: China to produce 142 mln tonnes of crude in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to produce 142 mln tonnes of crude in 1997.

text.p: China expects to produce 142 million tonnes of crude oil (equivalent to some 2.84 million barrels per day) and 17 billion cubic metres of natural gas on land this year, Zhou Yongkang, general manager of the China Oil and Gas Corp, said on Friday.
China expected to verify 530 million tonnes of geological oil reserves, the Xinhua news agency quoted him as saying at a meeting.
Oil prospecting would be given top priority this year to try to sustain increases in reserves and output, he said.
Existing oilfields in eastern China would try to maintain their current production levels, while western areas would strive to boost oil and gas output, he said.
China's largest Daqing oilfield would try to ensure output would remain steady at 56 million tonnes.
Shengli oilfield in eastern Shandong province would try to keep output at 28 million tonnes.
Northeastern Liaohe oilfield aimed to keep oil output at 15 million tonnes.
Northeastern Jilin oilfield would try to boost oil production capacity to produce 3.8 million tonnes of crude while Huabei, Dagang, Zhongyuan and Jidong oilfields would try to maintain steady output.
The Xinjiang and Changqing oilfields in western China would aim to produce 8.7 million tonnes and 3.2 million tonnes of oil respectively.

Xinjiang's Tarim oilfield was expected to produce 4.4 million tonnes, up by 1.3 million tonnes over 1996. The Turpan-Hami field was expected to make new finds and to produce 3.0 million tonnes this year, Zhou said.

In natural gas production, China aimed to complete the first-phase construction of a field in northern Shaanxi province, with a production capacity of 1.5 billion cubic metres and would build another field with a production capacity of 2.0 billion cubic metres in southwestern Sichuan Province, he said.
